clinician.final_diagnosis: mucosal-dominant pemphigus vulgaris with minimal skin lesions
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 90-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of painful gingivae and multiple erosions and vesicles on the oral mucosa, positive Nikolsky's sign, and a few erythematous erosions on the back. Oral mucosa biopsy showed intraepithelial suprabasal cleavage with acantholysis and basal keratinocyte retention. Direct immunofluorescence revealed IgG and C3 deposition between epithelial cells. Serological testing detected elevated anti-desmoglein 3 and anti-desmoglein 1 antibodies. These findings confirmed mucosal-dominant pemphigus vulgaris with minimal skin involvement.
